housing.text: On her campaign site she calls housing a basic human right and prioritizes expanding affordable and permanent housing, and as an Assemblymember she has authored bills to boost housing production.
housing.quote: Safe and affordable housing is a basic human right.

schools.text: Her platform prioritizes increased and equitable funding for public school districts and reducing overcrowding rather than school choice or vouchers.
schools.quote: We must acknowledge and address overcrowding in schools and make funding schools a priority while investing fully and equitably in students.

abortion.text: After Roe v. Wade was overturned she publicly decried the loss of abortion rights and called for a protest boycott.
abortion.quote: Lastly, last Friday women's reproductive rights were taken away!

energy.text: Her platform states California should lead in reaching net-zero greenhouse gas emissions and reducing carbon pollution, and she earned a 76% environmental voting score in 2025.
energy.quote: California must lead in being a net zero greenhouse gas emission state.

tax.text: Webb pledges to oppose every proposed tax increase and says California should reduce spending instead.
tax.quote: I will vote against every proposed tax increase. We have a spending problem, not a revenue problem.

housing.text: Webb advocates reducing regulatory barriers to housing and supports placing time limits on environmental reviews to advance new projects.
housing.quote: This Proposition will end the permanent pocket veto of housing projects by individuals in public agencies. One year is plenty long enough for due diligence in environmental impact reviews. This Proposition will promote housing in California.

energy.text: Webb wants to drop gas and diesel excise taxes and eliminate cap-and-trade and California's special fuel blend to lower energy costs.
energy.quote: Gas excise taxes and diesel excise taxes should be dropped as too regressive.

voting.text: Webb calls for a state voter ID law, regular voter-roll maintenance, and paper ballots with audits.
voting.quote: California should enact its own voter ID law before the federal government imposes one on us.
